title: ACT ON THE RESTORATION OF HONOR OF AND COMPENSATION TO PERSONS RELATED TO THE BUSAN-MASAN DEMOCRATIC UPRISING
title_original: 부마민주항쟁 관련자의 명예회복 및 보상 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the enhancement of human rights, democratic development, and national harmony by ascertaining the truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, restoring the honor of persons related thereto and their bereaved family members through the State, and providing substantial compensation to such persons and their bereaved family members accordingly.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. "Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising" means the democratization movement that occurred against the Yushin regime in Busan, Masan, Changwon, and other areas of Gyeongsangnam-do around the period from October 16 through October 20, 1979;
  2. "Related person" means any of the following persons who has been deliberated upon and determined by the Deliberative Commission for Ascertaining the Truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and Restoring the Honor of Related Persons under Article 4:
  a. A person who died or went missing in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  b. A person who was injured in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  c. A person who is recognized as having suffered from a disease prescribed by Presidential Decree in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising or as having died from the aftereffects thereof;
  d. A person who was wanted, arrested, or detained in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  e. A person who was subject to dismissal of prosecution, a conviction, judgment of acquittal, dismissal from office, or academic discipline in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  3. "Relevant institutions, etc." means other relevant institutions, facilities, and organizations related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, excluding reporting persons and persons subject to investigation.

Article 3 (Scope of bereaved families) (1) "Bereaved family members" in this Act means persons who inherit the property of a related person under the Civil Act; provided, in cases of a missing person, persons who would have inherited his or her property under the Civil Act at the time he or she went missing shall be deemed bereaved family members.
  (2) Bereaved family members jointly hold the right to receive monetary compensation and livelihood support grants prescribed by this Act according to their respective shares of inheritance under the Civil Act.

Article 4 (Deliberative Commission for Ascertaining the Truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and Restoring the Honor of Related Persons) (1) In order to perform the duties prescribed by this Act, the Deliberative Commission for Ascertaining the Truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and Restoring the Honor of Related Persons (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") shall be established under the jurisdiction of the Prime Minister.
  (2) The functions of the Commission shall be as follows:
  1. Ascertaining the truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  2. Deliberating on and determining whether a person qualifies as a related person or his or her bereaved family member;
  3. Determining disability ratings of related persons who sustained injuries;
  4. Matters concerning the deliberation, determination, and payment of monetary compensation, etc. to related persons and bereaved family members;
  5. Preparing financial measures for compensation, etc. for related persons or their bereaved family members;
  6. Matters necessary for restoring the honor of related persons and bereaved family members;
  7. Supporting memorial projects for related persons, including the establishment of memorial facilities;
  8. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree in connection with ascertaining the truth, restoring honor, compensation, etc.

Article 5 (Composition of Commission) (1) The Commission shall consist of not more than 15 commissioners, including 1 standing commissioner.
  (2) The commissioners shall be appointed or commissioned by the President from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience, including 1 person recommended by each of the following: the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Busan Metropolitan City Mayor, the Gyeongsangnam-do Governor, the Mayor of the Changwon-si, and organizations associated with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising in Busan and Changwon. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
  (3) The Chairperson shall be elected by and from among the commissioners of the Commission.
  (4) The term of office of the Chairperson and commissioners shall be 2 years, and they may be reappointed or recommissioned only once.
  (5) Other matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the Commission shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Period for ascertaining truth about Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising) (1) The Commission shall complete activities for ascertaining the truth about the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, including the collection and analysis of related materials, within 1 year from the enforcement date of this Act (referring to July 27, 2022, the enforcement date of the partially amended Act on the Restoration of Honor of and Compensation to Persons Related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising under Act No. 18845). <Amended on Dec. 24, 2018; Jun. 9, 2020; Apr. 26, 2022>
  (2) If the Commission finds it impracticable to complete activities for ascertaining the truth within the period prescribed in paragraph (1), it may report thereon to the President and the National Assembly 3 months before the expiration of such period and extend the period within the scope of 1 year. <Added on Apr. 26, 2022>

Article 7 (Reporting for ascertaining truth) (1) The Commission shall open reporting centers in Busan Metropolitan City, Gyeongsangnam-do, etc. to receive reports on facts, damages, etc. for ascertaining the truth, and shall make a public announcement thereof.
  (2) A related person, a bereaved family member thereof, a person in a familial relationship therewith, or a person who has knowledge of specific facts concerning truth-ascertainment may submit a report to the Commission.
  (3) The scope of persons in a familial relationship and persons who have knowledge of specific facts under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Methods of investigation for ascertaining truth) The Commission may take any of the following measures in conducting an investigation:
  1. Requesting reporting persons and persons subject to investigation to submit written statements;
  2. Requesting reporting persons and persons subject to investigation to attend and hearing their statements;
  3. Requesting reporting persons, persons subject to investigation, and relevant institutions, etc. to submit related materials or articles, and taking custody of the submitted materials;
  4. Inquiring with relevant institutions, etc. about facts or information recognized as being related to the matters under investigation.
  5. Designating an expert witness and requesting him or her to conduct appraisal.

Article 8-2 (Orders to accompany) (1) If a person requested to attend under subparagraph 2 of Article 8, who is deemed to possess conclusive evidential materials or information regarding an investigation by the Commission, fails to comply with such request without good cause on at least 2 occasions, the Commission may, by its resolution, issue a written order to accompany requiring the person to accompany.
  (2) A written order to accompany under paragraph (1) shall state the name and residence of the person subject thereto, the grounds for the order to accompany, the place to which the person shall be brought, the date of issuance, the period of validity of the warrant, a statement to the effect that the warrant shall not be executed after the expiration of such period and shall be returned, and a statement to the effect that an administrative fine shall be imposed where the person refuses to comply with the order to accompany, and the warrant shall be signed and sealed by the Chairperson. When the name of the person subject thereto is uncertain, the person may be identified by description of appearance, physique, or other identifying characteristics; and where the residence is uncertain, the statement of residence may be omitted.
  (3) A written order to accompany shall be served by presenting it to the relevant person subject to the order to accompany.
  (4) A written order to accompany shall be served by a staff member of the Commission.
  (5) A written order to accompany against a person detained in a prison or a detention center (including a military prison or a military detention center) shall be executed by a correctional officer under delegation by a staff member of the Commission.
  (6) Where the relevant person is an active-duty soldier in a military camp, the commander of the unit to which the person belongs shall be obligated to cooperate with a staff member of the Commission in the service of the written order to accompany on such person.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 9 (Fact-finding investigation and duty to cooperate) (1) For compensation, etc. under this Act, the Commission may hear testimony or statements from related persons, witnesses, or reference witnesses and, where deemed necessary, may conduct verifications or other necessary investigations, and may request necessary cooperation from administrative agencies and other relevant institutions. In such cases, the administrative agencies and other relevant institutions requested to cooperate shall give priority to such request over other duties and notify the Commission of the results without delay. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2018>
  (2) The Commission may, only for investigations under paragraph (1), request relevant institutions, including the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Supreme Court, to submit materials concerning personal information, including resident registration data and family relation registration data. In such cases, the relevant institutions requested to do so shall submit such materials. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2018>

Article 10 (Preparation of fact-finding reports) (1) The Commission shall prepare a fact-finding report on the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising (hereinafter referred to as the "fact-finding report") within 6 months from the date on which the period prescribed in Article 6 expires.
  (2) A fact-finding report shall include a list of related persons.
  (3) The Commission shall, upon completing the preparation of a fact-finding report, publish it in the Official Gazette and make a public announcement thereof.

Article 10-2 (Ex officio determination of related persons by Commission) (1) The Commission may determine any participant in the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising who is specified in a fact-finding report as falling under any of the items of subparagraph 2 of Article 2 to be a related person without a separate application. In such cases, the Commission shall notify the participant specified in the fact-finding report of the fact of falling under the category of a related person in advance and obtain his or her consent.
  (2) With respect to a person who is not specified as a participant in the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising in a fact-finding report, the Commission shall deliberate on the person upon application.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]

Article 11 (Special retrial) (1) Notwithstanding Articles 420 and 424 of the Criminal Procedure Act and Articles 469 and 473 of the Military Court Act, a related person who has received a final and conclusive judgment of conviction or judgment of acquittal in connection with acts related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising may file a petition for retrial.
  (2) A petition for a retrial shall be under the jurisdiction of the court that rendered the original judgment; provided, if the court that rendered the original judgment against a person to whom the Military Criminal Act does not apply is a court-martial or a military court, the court having jurisdiction over the person's place of residence corresponding to that instance of trial shall have jurisdiction.
  (3) Where a petitioner for retrial who has received a final and conclusive judgment of conviction has been pardoned or the sentence has become invalid, the court having jurisdiction over the retrial shall render a final judgment on the merits notwithstanding Articles 326 through 328 of the Criminal Procedure Act and Articles 381 through 383 of the Military Court Act. The same shall also apply to a petitioner for retrial who has received a judgment of acquittal by reason of exemption from prosecution.
  (4) The procedures for retrials under paragraph (1) shall be subject to the application of the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Act and the Military Court Act as long as they are not against the nature of the relevant retrial.

Article 12 (Issuance of certificates of related persons) (1) The Commission shall issue a certificate of a related person to a person who has been determined to be a related person.
  (2) The Commission shall publish the facts determined in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising in the Official Gazette and make a public announcement thereof in 2 or more daily newspapers.

Article 13 (Recommendation for reinstatement) Where a related person so desires, the Commission may recommend that the State, a local government, or an employer reinstate the related person who was dismissed from employment.

Article 14 (Recommendation for expungement of academic disciplinary records) The Commission may recommend to the school attended by a related person the expungement of such related person's academic disciplinary records related to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, the readmission of such related person, and the conferment of an honorary diploma thereon.

Article 15 (Prohibition of disadvantageous treatment) No person recognized as a related person under this Act shall be subject to any discriminatory treatment or disadvantage from the State, local governments, employers, etc. on the ground that he or she was involved in the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising.

Article 16 (Support for foundations related to Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising) (1) The Government may support necessary expenses within the scope of the budget or contribute funds to a foundation established for the purpose of carrying out memorial projects, etc. for the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising (hereafter in this Article referred to as the "foundation").
  (2) A foundation that intends to receive support under paragraph (1) shall apply for support for project expenses, etc. as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The provisions concerning incorporated foundations in the Civil Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the operation of foundations.
  (4) Other matters necessary for the operation, etc. of foundations shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 17 (Acceptance of donated goods or money) (1) Notwithstanding the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 5(2) of the Act on Collection and Use of Donations, the Commission may accept voluntarily donated money or goods within the scope consistent with its business purposes.
  (2) Matters necessary for the procedures, etc. for accepting donated money and goods under Paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Restrictions on organization of support groups for related persons) No person shall, under the pretext of supporting a related person or his or her bereaved family or family member, organize an organization, engage in collective or individual activities for profit-making purposes.

Article 19 (Compensation for related persons) (1) Monetary compensation shall be paid to any person recognized as a related person under this Act.
  (2) Compensation under this Act shall be deemed compensation for damages.

Article 20 (Principles of compensation) Related persons and their bereaved family members shall be compensated according to the extent of sacrifice suffered by the related persons; provided, the amount of compensation may vary in consideration of their standard of living.

Article 21 (Monetary compensation) (1) A related person or his or her bereaved family members shall be paid monetary compensation in an amount calculated in accordance with the following classifications, plus interest accrued at the statutory interest rate until the determination on compensation is made:
  1. For bereaved family members of a person confirmed to have died or gone missing in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, an amount obtained by deducting intermediate interest therefrom under the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate from the amount obtained by multiplying the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage at the time of death or disappearance by the future employable period;
  2. For a person injured in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising or his or her bereaved family members, an amount equal to the sum of the following amounts:
  a. Where necessary medical care causes a loss of income from the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage: the amount of such loss during the period of medical care;
  b. Where the injured person has a physical disability: an amount obtained by multiplying the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage at the time the injury was sustained by the rate of loss of labor capacity and the future employable period according to the degree of disability resulting therefrom, and deducting intermediate interest therefrom under the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate.
  (2) If a person who sustained an injury in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising dies from a cause other than such injury, monetary compensation shall be paid under paragraph (1)2 by deeming such person to be alive.
  (3) The monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage under paragraph (1) shall be based on a certificate issued by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the place of residence, the head of a tax office, or any other reliable certification; and where it cannot be certified, it shall be determined as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) In calculating monetary compensation under Paragraph (1), living expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be deducted from the amount of the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage.
  (5) The future employable period, disability ratings, and rates of loss of labor capacity under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 21-2 (Adjustment and payment of monetary compensation) Where there is a substantial difference between the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage at the time of death or injury and the monthly wage, monthly net income, or average wage at the time the determination on compensation is made, monetary compensation may be adjusted and paid as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on May 29, 2016]

Article 22 (Livelihood support grants) (1) The Commission may pay support money for assisting the livelihood of the following persons and their bereaved family members:
  1. A person detained for not less than 30 days on the ground of the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising;
  2. A person injured or suffering from a disease in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising whose degree of injury or disease is minor and who is therefore not eligible for compensation under Article 21(1)2b or Article 21(2);
  3. A dismissed person whose period of employment is not less than 1 year.
  (2) Livelihood support grants under paragraph (1) may be paid from money and goods voluntarily contributed for supporting related persons, and the Government may support part of the financial resources therefor.
  (3) Matters necessary for the criteria for payment, amounts, methods of payment, etc. of livelihood support grants shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 23 (Medical support grants) (1) For any person who sustained an injury in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising and who, at the time this Act enters into force, requires continuous medical treatment, constant care, or the use of assistive devices due to such injury, expenses actually incurred for medical treatment, care, and the purchase of assistive devices shall be paid in a lump sum as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) In paying medical support grants under paragraph (1), intermediate interest shall be deducted therefrom under the simple discount method at the statutory interest rate.
  (3) Medical expenses already borne by a person who sustained an injury in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising shall be reimbursed. In such cases, the standards and methods of payment shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 24 (Application for payment of monetary compensation, etc.) (1) A related person or his or her bereaved family member intending to receive monetary compensation, livelihood support grants, or medical support grants under this Act (hereinafter referred to as "monetary compensation, etc.") shall apply in writing to the Commission for payment of monetary compensation, etc., attaching relevant supporting documents thereto, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) An application for payment of monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1) shall be filed within 6 months after the applicant is determined to be a related person or bereaved family member.

Article 25 (Deliberation and decision) The Commission shall determine whether to pay monetary compensation, etc. and the amount thereof within 90 days from the date it receives an application for the payment of monetary compensation, etc.; provided, in the case of a missing person, such decision shall be made within 120 days.

Article 26 (Service of written decision) (1) Where the Commission determines to pay or not to pay monetary compensation, etc., it shall serve an authentic copy of the written decision on the applicant within 30 days.
  (2) The provisions of the Civil Procedure Act regarding service shall apply mutatis mutandis to service under paragraph (1).

Article 27 (Redeliberation) (1) A related person or his or her bereaved family member who objects to a decision of the Commission under the main clause of Article 25 may apply to the Commission for redeliberation within 30 days from the date on which an authentic copy of the written decision under Article 26 is served on him or her.
  (2) Articles 25 and 26 shall apply mutatis mutandis to redeliberation and service by the Commission. In such cases, "90 days" and "120 days" in Article 25 shall be deemed "60 days," respectively.

Article 28 (Consent of applicant and payment of monetary compensation, etc.) (1) When an applicant served with an authentic copy of the written decision under Article 26 intends to receive monetary compensation, etc., he or she shall, without delay, claim payment of monetary compensation, etc. from the Commission by attaching thereto a written consent to such decision.
  (2) Matters necessary for the procedures, etc. of payment of monetary compensation, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29 (Protection of right to receive monetary compensation, etc.) The right to receive payment of monetary compensation, etc. under this Act shall not be transferred, provided as collateral, or seized.

Article 30 (Tax exemption) No national or local tax shall be imposed on monetary compensation, etc. under this Act.

Article 31 (Requirement of prior determination) (1) No lawsuit concerning the payment of monetary compensation, etc. under this Act may be filed unless a decision has been rendered by the Commission to pay or dismiss monetary compensation, etc.; provided, this shall not apply where 90 days have elapsed from the date on which an application for payment of monetary compensation, etc. is filed.
  (2) A lawsuit under paragraph (1) shall be filed within 60 days from the date on which the authentic copy of the written decision (including the authentic copy of a written decision on reconsideration) under Article 26 is served.

Article 32 (Relationship with compensation under other statutes) (1) Where a person has received compensation or damages from the State or a local government under the Act on the Honor Restoration of and Compensation to Persons Related to Democratization Movements or the State Compensation Act in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising, monetary compensation, etc. under this Act shall be paid after deducting such compensation or damages therefrom. <Amended on May 18, 2015>
  (2) Where an applicant agrees to a decision to pay monetary compensation, etc. under this Act under Article 28, a judicial compromise under the Civil Procedure Act shall be deemed to have been established with respect to damages incurred in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising.

Article 33 (Recovery of monetary compensation, etc.) (1) Where a person who has received monetary compensation, etc. pursuant to this Act falls under any of the following cases, the State may recover all or part of the monetary compensation, etc. that he or she has received; provided, the entire monetary compensation, etc. shall be recovered in cases falling under subparagraph 1:
  1. Where he or she has received monetary compensation, etc. by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where he or she was erroneously paid;
  3. Where a person confirmed as missing in connection with the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising is found to be alive, or is found to have died or gone missing for reasons unrelated to the Busan-Masan Democratic Uprising.
  (2) Where the State recovers monetary compensation, etc. under paragraph (1), it shall do so in accordance with the practices applicable to dispositions on default of national taxes.

Article 34 (Prescription) The right to receive monetary compensation, etc. under this Act shall become extinct if not exercised within 3 years from the date an authentic copy of a written determination of the payment of monetary compensation, etc. is served on the applicant; provided, where a lawsuit seeking the payment of monetary compensation, etc. under this Act is instituted, prescription shall be suspended from the date such lawsuit is instituted until the date a final and conclusive judgment is issued.

Article 35 (Penalty provisions) (1) Any person who receives or causes another person to receive monetary compensation, etc. under this Act by fraud or other improper means shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 5 years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won.
  (2) A person who attempts to commit the offense under paragraph (1) shall be punished.
  (3) Any person who violates Article 18 shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 36 (Administrative fines) (1) Any person who fails to comply with an order to accompany issued under Article 8-2 without good cause shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won.
  (2) The administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Chairperson, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 9, 2020]
